stages: Capture out_values.dtype if no dtype was supplied
Bind the current np.max callable before fetching its keys argument
Compute the maximum and scalar +1 before allocation
Invoke the previously bound allocator with length and dtype keyword
Fetch fresh out_values first, then fresh in_values
Assign through validated native scatter or checked __setitem__ and return the same allocator result
ordinary_integer_max: Retains C++ scan for exact plain ndarray with a built-in integer dtype and the unchanged canonical NumPy max provider; other providers/protocols call the live max(keys) without an added axis keyword.
ordinary_assignment: Retains C++ duplicate-order scatter for exact plain arrays, writable C-contiguous one-dimensional output, matching built-in numeric contiguous values, valid snapshotted keys and disjoint output/value bytes.
checked_assignment: Strided, readonly, subclass, arbitrary __setitem__ output, unsupported dtype/protocol or overlapping value storage uses PyObject_SetItem. No implicit ndarray conversion of allocator output occurs.
private_pipeline: Actual changed consumer binding and unchanged native kernels, one private C++ worker state, explicit private bootstrap. Not complete production-package acceptance.
complete_package_acceptance: pending separate frozen883 SDK and complete22-binding product proof
unproven_scopes: Arbitrary mutation of NumPy implementation objects or private implementation globals while retaining callable identity
All possible user-defined dtype, descriptor, sequence and custom-output protocols beyond the bounded safe fixtures
Arbitrary custom allocator results propagated into lazy __setitem__ cache operations beyond the existing dense contract
Bounds-unsafe fabricated arrays or huge original allocations
